title: Quantification of Ethylene Production in Litchi Using Gas Chromatography
author: Regina B. Cronje
license_note: PMC full-text XML — Bio-protocol — CC-BY confirmed in article XML

steps.title: Set up GC hardware
steps.instruction: Install a 5 mm glass split liner with graphite seal into the split/splitless injector; place a 17 mm coated septum (Thermo Scientific 31303211) between septum support and holder and hand‑tighten the injector cap. Connect the TG‑BOND Q+ (Thermo 26005‑6030) capillary column (30 m × 0.32 mm × 10 µm) between the flame ionization detector (FID) and split liner using 0.32 mm graphite ferrules (Thermo 29053487), inserting 40 mm into the liner and 94 mm into the FID. Connect high‑purity He (99.999 %, Afrox 524203‑SE‑C) at 800 kPa to the GC. Verify gas‑generator pressures and flows: H₂ 420 kPa, 30–50 mL min⁻¹; dry air 420 kPa, 300–600 mL min⁻¹; N₂ 420 kPa, 10–60 mL min⁻¹ (Table 1). In the Xcaliber “Instrument Setup” page configure the parameters (Table 2): He carrier, split injector base 100 °C, split flow 40 mL min⁻¹, septum purge 5 mL min⁻¹, constant pressure 140 kPa, column length 30 m, diameter 0.32 mm, film 10 µm, oven start 60 °C (no ramp) to 60 °C, FID base 200 °C, H₂ flow 35 mL min⁻¹, air flow 350 mL min⁻¹, N₂ flow 30 mL min⁻¹, sampling depth 25 mm, syringe filling speed 50 mL min⁻¹, injection speed 50 mL min⁻¹, injection depth 50 mm, needle penetration 25 mm s⁻¹.

steps.title: Configure GC software processing
steps.instruction: In Thermo Xcaliber open “Processing Setup”, import a *.raw file representing a low‑concentration C₂H₄ injection, and set the processing variables as in Table 3: analog detector, peak detect ICIS, expected time 1.64 min, window 5 s, view width 0.75, smoothing points 1, baseline window 60, area noise 5, peak noise 10, highest peak, minimum S/N 3.0, calibration component target compound, weighting equal, linear units nL, origin ignore, response area levels 1–11 with values 0.075, 0.150, 0.301, 0.752, 1.505, 3.010, 8.809, 16.709, 24.609, 44.359, 83.859.

steps.title: Create calibration and sample sequences
steps.instruction: Using Xcaliber “Sequence Setup”, create a sequence file with 11 entries for calibration standards, referencing the instrument method under “Inst Meth” and the processing method under “Proc Meth”, and specifying the calibration file path under “Cal File”. Then create a separate sequence for the experimental samples, also linking the calibration file. Note that tray slot positions are required only for standards 1‑6; sample injections will be performed manually.

steps.title: Collect plant material and seal vials
steps.instruction: Detach two leaflets from each terminal shoot of a litchi compound leaf at the natural abscission layer and remove up to 20 terminal buds (4–8 mm long) with sharp Iris scissors. Place leaflets into 20 mL crimp‑top headspace vials (Thermo CHCV20‑14) and buds into 1.8 mL screw‑top vials (Cronus VZS‑0209C‑100). Record the harvest time for each vial. Leave vials open for 10.0 ± 0.5 min at ambient conditions to allow wound ethylene release. After equilibration, seal 20 mL vials with 20 mm Si/PTFE septa (Cronus VCS‑2004‑1000) and 20 mm aluminum crimp caps (Cronus VCC‑2002CS‑1000) using the 20 mm hand crimper (Cronus VTC‑20), ensuring the PTFE face contacts the vial wall. Hand‑tighten the screw caps on the 2 mL vials. Record the sealing time as the start of the 3‑h incubation.

steps.title: Prepare calibration standards 1‑6
steps.instruction: Seal six 20 mL headspace vials with magnetic crimp caps (Cronus VCC‑2002BM‑500) and Si/PTFE septa. Connect a two‑stage regulator to a 79 µL L⁻¹ C₂H₄/N₂ cylinder (Afrox GOC mix 3292). Close the cylinder shut‑off valve, turn the regulator control knob fully counter‑clockwise (outlet closed), open and close the cylinder valve to charge the inlet, then turn the knob clockwise until the low‑pressure gauge reads 50 kPa (do not exceed 100 kPa). Purge the regulator three times: insert a 23 G 51 mm Hamilton needle (7729‑06) through the low‑pressure outlet septum, watch the high‑pressure gauge fall toward zero, withdraw the needle just before the low‑pressure gauge reaches zero, then repeat the charge‑purge cycle two more times. Using 100 µL (Thermo 36520050) and 2 500 µL (Thermo 365Q2131) gastight syringes, aspirate the volumes listed in Table 4 (e.g., 20 µL, 40 µL, 80 µL, 200 µL, 400 µL, 800 µL) from the regulator, extracting slightly more than required and then retracting the plunger to the exact volume to eliminate pressure effects. Inject 1 mL of each prepared standard into the GC with the Triplus autosampler using the headspace tool (needle insertion depth 50 mm).

steps.title: Prepare calibration standards 7‑11
steps.instruction: Using a 2 500 µL gastight syringe (Thermo 365Q2131) with a dead volume of 61.5 µL, aspirate the volumes in Table 5 (50, 150, 250, 500, 1 000 µL) from the same C₂H₄ cylinder. After each aspiration, move the plunger back to the 1 000 µL mark to dilute the gas with air (in‑situ dilution). Manually inject 1 mL of each diluted standard into the GC, limiting needle insertion depth to 50 mm. Calculate the injected C₂H₄ volume (V’_inj‑IS) using equation 4 and the dead‑volume value.

steps.title: Prepare blanks and QC standards
steps.instruction: Seal four 20 mL headspace vials with ambient air using aluminum crimp caps and Si/PTFE septa, and seal four 2 mL screw‑top vials with ambient air. For C₂H₄ QC standards, use a 100 µL gastight syringe to aspirate 20 µL (for 2 mL vials) and 80 µL (for 20 mL vials) of the C₂H₄ cylinder gas, employing the excess‑volume technique, and inject into the respective vials (three technical replicates each, Table 6). Sample the QC vials with disposable 3 mL syringes (generic) equipped with 23 G 51 mm needles and luer locks: aspirate 1 mL from each 20 mL vial and 0.5 mL from each 2 mL vial, cycling the required volume twice with the needle stationary before final aspiration, and keep the luer valve closed while holding the plunger. Flush the needle with a clean 3 mL syringe between vials. Manually inject the QC samples into the GC, inserting the needle fully (51 mm) to match the programmed 50 mm injection depth.

steps.title: Sample ethylene from plant vials
steps.instruction: Exactly 3.00 ± 0.05 h after sealing, withdraw gas from each plant vial using a disposable 3 mL syringe with a 23 G 51 mm needle and luer lock. Aspirate 1 mL from 20 mL vials and 0.5 mL from 2 mL vials, using the same cycling technique as for QC samples, ensuring the needle does not contact leaf or bud material (leaves rest against vial wall, buds avoided by visual control). Keep the luer valve closed while holding the plunger, record the sampling time, flush the needle between vials, and manually inject the sample into the GC with the needle inserted to 50 mm depth.

steps.title: Weigh vials and calculate release
steps.instruction: After chromatography, remove caps from the 20 mL vials with pliers and unscrew the 2 mL vial caps. Weigh each sealed vial with its plant material, then remove the plant material and weigh the empty vial. Use these masses together with the measured C₂H₄ peak areas to calculate ethylene release normalized to unit plant mass (per Equation 5).
